Let  

\[
U\;:=\;\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb Z[a,b,\,\Delta^{-1}]\Bigr)
\qquad\text{with}\qquad 
\Delta(a,b)=\operatorname{disc}\bigl(x^{5}+a x+b\bigr).
\]

Thus a point \(u=(a,b)\in U(R)\) for a commutative ring \(R\) corresponds to the monic
quintic polynomial  

\[
f_{u}(x)=x^{5}+a x+b\in R[x]
\]

which is separable (the discriminant is invertible) and whose discriminant is a **square**
in \(R\).  Consequently the Galois group of the generic fibre of the morphism  

\[
\pi : Z\longrightarrow U ,\qquad 
Z\;:=\;\bigl\{(a,b,x)\mid f_{a,b}(x)=0\bigr\}\subset U\times \mathbf A^{1}
\]

lies inside the alternating group \(A_{5}\); in fact it equals \(A_{5}\) after base‑change
to \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) (this is the classical “icosahedral’’ construction of
generic \(A_{5}\)‑extensions).

Let \(\bar\pi : Z_{\overline{\eta}}\to U_{\overline{\eta}}\) be the geometric generic fibre.
Since \(\Delta\neq 0\), \(\bar\pi\) is finite étale of degree \(5\), and the
geometric fundamental group \(\pi_{1}^{\text{ét}}(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})\) acts on the
geometric fibre \(\bar\pi^{-1}(\bar\eta)\cong\{1,\dots ,5\}\) via the natural
faithful transitive action of the group  

\[
G:=\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\pi_{1}^{\text{ét}}(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})
   \longrightarrow \operatorname{Aut}\{1,\dots ,5\}\bigr)=A_{5}.
\]

For a prime number \(p\neq 2,5\) let  

\[
U_{p}=U\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_{p},\qquad 
\pi_{p}: Z_{p}=Z\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_{p}\longrightarrow U_{p}
\]

be the reductions modulo \(p\).  The morphism \(\pi_{p}\) is still finite étale of degree 5
over the open subscheme where the discriminant is invertible, and its fibres are
zero‑dimensional reduced schemes.

For a rational point \(u\in U_{p}(\mathbb F_{p})\) write  

\[
X_{u}:=\pi_{p}^{-1}(u)=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb F_{p}[x]/(f_{u}(x))\Bigr) .
\]

The scheme \(X_{u}\) is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field
extensions of \(\mathbb F_{p}\); its **connected components over \(\mathbb F_{p}\)**
are precisely the orbits of the absolute Frobenius \(\mathrm{Frob}_{p}\) on the
geometric fibre \(\bar X_{u}\cong\{1,\dots ,5\}\).  Hence

\[
\#X_{u}\;=\;\text{number of cycles of the permutation }
      \sigma_{u}\in A_{5}\subset S_{5}
\]
induced by \(\mathrm{Frob}_{p}\) on \(\bar X_{u}\).

Define

\[
L\;:=\;\lim_{p\to\infty}
        \frac{1}{\#U_{p}(\mathbb F_{p})}
        \sum_{u\in U_{p}(\mathbb F_{p})}\#X_{u}.
\tag{1}
\]

(The limit exists because the complement of the étale locus has codimension \(1\) in
\(U\) and therefore contributes a negligible proportion of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points.)

and that the induced action on the eight geometric roots of \(F(t,x)\) is the

\[

Let \(f(x)=x^{5}+a_{4}x^{4}+a_{3}x^{3}+a_{2}x^{2}+a_{1}x+a_{0}\) be a monic polynomial of degree 5 with coefficients in the finite field \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\), where \(p\) is a prime.  
Assume that the Galois group of the splitting field of \(f\) over \(\mathbb{F}_{p}(x)\) is the full symmetric group \(S_{5}\) (this holds for a density‑one set of such polynomials as \(p\to\infty\)).  

For a given polynomial \(f\), let \(N_{p}(f)\) denote the number of roots of \(f\) in \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\) (i.e. the number of linear factors of \(f\) over \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)).  

Define
\[
L \;=\; \lim_{p\to\infty}\;\frac{1}{\#\{f\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]\text{ monic, degree }5,\ \operatorname{Gal}(f)=S_{5}\}}\;
\sum_{\substack{f\text{ monic, degree }5\\ \operatorname{Gal}(f)=S_{5}}} N_{p}(f).
\]

Compute \(\displaystyle \bigl\lfloor 100\,L\bigr\rfloor\).

(Answer should be given as an integer.)

Let \(S_{7}\) act on the set \(X\) of all functions \(f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to\{1,2,\dots ,7\}\) by permuting the values:
\[
(\sigma\cdot f)(i)=\sigma\bigl(f(i)\bigr)\qquad(\sigma\in S_{7},\;i=1,2,3,4).
\]
For a permutation \(\sigma\in S_{7}\), a function \(f\in X\) is fixed by \(\sigma\) precisely when
\(\sigma\) fixes each value in the multiset \(\{f(1),f(2),f(3),f(4)\}\).

Let \(F(\sigma)\) denote the number of functions in \(X\) fixed by \(\sigma\).
Define
\[
L=\frac{1}{|S_{7}|}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{7}}F(\sigma),
\]
the average number of fixed functions of a random permutation of \(S_{7}\) acting on \(X\).

Compute \(\displaystyle \big\lfloor 100\,L\big\rfloor\).  (Give the integer result.)

Let \(k=\mathbb{F}_p\) be a finite field of odd characteristic.  
Consider five homogeneous quadratic polynomials \(Q_1,\dots,Q_5\) in six variables
\(X_0,\dots,X_5\) with coefficients chosen uniformly at random from \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
Let \(V\subset\mathbb{P}^5_k\) be the projective variety defined by the simultaneous
vanishing of the \(Q_i\):
\[
V:\; Q_1=Q_2=Q_3=Q_4=Q_5=0.
\]

For each prime \(p\) let
\[
N(p)=\#\bigl\{\,x\in\mathbb{P}^5(\mathbb{F}_p)\mid x\in V(\mathbb{F}_p)\,\bigr\},
\]
the number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-rational points of the (zero‑dimensional) scheme
\(V\) (counted without multiplicity).  
Define
\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p^{5}}\sum_{Q_1,\dots,Q_5}
\frac{N(p)}{p-1},
\]
where the sum runs over all choices of the five quadrics (up to scaling of each
quadratic form, i.e. over \(\mathbb{P}^{20}(\mathbb{F}_p)\) for each \(Q_i\)),
so that the denominator \(p^{5}\) is the total number of choices of the five
quadrics up to scaling, and the factor \(p-1\) accounts for the projective
scaling of points in \(\mathbb{P}^5(\mathbb{F}_p)\).

In other words, \(L\) is the average number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-rational points of
the complete intersection of five random quadrics in \(\mathbb{P}^5\), in the limit
as \(p\) grows.

Compute \(\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).

the limit of the average number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-rational points of \(X_a\) as \(a\) ranges over \(\mathbb{F}_p\).  Compute \(\displaystyle\big\lfloor 100\,L\big\rfloor\).

Let \(U\subset \mathbf P^{5}\) be the open subset parametrising smooth plane conics (i.e. the complement of the discriminant hypersurface).  
For a conic \(C\) denote by \([C]\in U\) its point in this parameter space.  

A line \(\ell\subset\mathbf P^{2}\) is tangent to a conic \(C\) if \(\ell\) meets \(C\) with multiplicity 2 at some point.  
Fix a finite field \(\mathbf F_{p}\) with odd prime \(p\).  

Consider the following set of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-rational lines:
\[
\mathcal L_{p}=\Bigl\{\ell\subset\mathbf P^{2}_{\mathbf F_{p}}\;\Big|\;
\ell\text{ is tangent to each of four given smooth conics }
C_{1},C_{2},C_{3},C_{4}\in U(\mathbf F_{p})\Bigr\}.
\]

It is a classical fact that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic
\(\neq2\) a generic quadruple of smooth conics has exactly \(16\) (geometrically
distinct) common tangent lines, counted with multiplicity.

Let \(V\subset U^{4}\) be the dense open subset of quadruples \((C_{1},\dots ,C_{4})\) for which the above tangency conditions are transverse, so that \(\#\mathcal L_{p}=16\) over the algebraic closure.

Define
\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\sum_{(C_{1},\dots ,C_{4})\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\mathcal L_{p},
\]
the limit of the average number of (geometric) common tangent lines to four
smooth conics over \(\mathbf F_{p}\) as \(p\) grows.

Compute \(\displaystyle\bigl\lfloor 100\,L\bigr\rfloor\).

(Answer as a decimal integer.)

For a given \((F,G,H)\in\mathcal{A}(\mathbb F_{p})\) let
\[
N_{p}(F,G,H)=\#\bigl( V(F)\cap V(G)\cap V(H) \bigr)(\mathbb F_{p}),

the number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-rational points in the (geometric) intersection of the three curves.

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\;
\frac{1}{\#\mathcal{A}(\mathbb F_{p})}
\sum_{(F,G,H)\in\mathcal{A}(\mathbb F_{p})}
N_{p}(F,G,H),
\]
the limit, as the prime \(p\) grows, of the average number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-rational points in the transverse intersection of a random conic, cubic, and quintic in the plane.

Compute \(\displaystyle \bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).
